title: CI/CD Artifacts and Advanced Pipeline Patterns
description: Personalized DOP-C02 training for CodeArtifact package events and promotion, CodePipeline cross-account and cross-Region artifact flow, CodeBuild dynamic artifacts and parallel tests, and immutable build-once release promotion.

topicDescriptors.title: CodeArtifact Package Events and Dependency Promotion
CodePipeline Cross-Account and Cross-Region Artifact Flow
CodeBuild Buildspec, Dynamic Artifacts, and Parallel Test Execution
Immutable Artifacts, Release Promotion, and Artifact Identity

conceptMaps.title: CodeArtifact package publication to pipeline flow

steps.label: 1. Publish or copy a package version
steps.detail: A build publishes a new package version or copies an approved version into another repository.

steps.label: 2. CodeArtifact emits an EventBridge event
steps.detail: The event identifies the domain, repository, package, version, state, operation type, and sequence number.

steps.label: 3. EventBridge filters the exact package event
steps.detail: The rule should match the intended repository, package name, version state, and operation instead of every CodeArtifact event.

steps.label: 4. Start the validation or release workflow
steps.detail: EventBridge can start CodePipeline directly or invoke Lambda or Step Functions when enrichment or orchestration is required.

steps.label: 5. Make processing idempotent
steps.detail: Use package identity, packageVersionRevision, or sequenceNumber to tolerate duplicates and out-of-order delivery.

conceptMaps.title: Cross-account action authorization and artifact flow

steps.label: 1. Pipeline account owns the pipeline and artifact store
steps.detail: The pipeline service role orchestrates actions and assumes a role in the target account.

steps.label: 2. Target account owns the action role
steps.detail: The role trust policy allows the pipeline service role to assume it, and its permissions policy authorizes the deployment resources.

steps.label: 3. Artifact bucket policy permits target-account access
steps.detail: The cross-account action and deployment resources must read the pipeline artifacts.

steps.label: 4. Customer-managed KMS key authorizes both sides
steps.detail: Cross-account artifact encryption requires key-policy and IAM permissions for the pipeline and target-account roles.

steps.label: 5. The action references roleArn and consumes allowed artifacts
steps.detail: Artifact flow must remain within CodePipeline cross-account limitations; arbitrary account-to-account passing outside the pipeline account is not supported.

steps.label: 1. Keep the pipeline in one home Region
steps.detail: The pipeline remains hosted in its original Region.

steps.label: 2. Define one artifact store per action Region
steps.detail: Each cross-Region action Region needs an S3 artifact bucket and optional KMS key in the pipeline account.

steps.label: 3. Set the Region on the action
steps.detail: The action references deployment or build resources that exist in that Region.

steps.label: 4. CodePipeline copies input artifacts
steps.detail: CodePipeline replicates the input artifact to the action Region automatically.

steps.label: 5. Respect unsupported action categories
steps.detail: Source, third-party, and custom actions cannot be configured as cross-Region actions.

conceptMaps.title: Fast and traceable CodeBuild test stage

steps.label: 1. Define commands and outputs in buildspec
steps.detail: The buildspec controls phases, environment variables, reports, caching, and artifacts.

steps.label: 2. Derive artifact identity from pipeline or source metadata
steps.detail: Branch, commit, build number, or release version can become artifact names and metadata.

steps.label: 3. Run independent actions in parallel
steps.detail: CodePipeline actions in the same stage with the same runOrder execute in parallel.

steps.label: 4. Publish test reports and artifacts
steps.detail: CodeBuild report groups and output artifacts make failures and evidence visible.

steps.label: 5. Gate promotion on successful completion
steps.detail: The next stage starts only after the required parallel actions succeed.

conceptMaps.title: Build once, verify, and promote the same artifact

steps.label: 1. Build one release artifact
steps.detail: Create the binary, package, image, SDK, or infrastructure bundle once.

steps.label: 2. Assign immutable identity
steps.detail: Use a package version, S3 version, object checksum, or container digest rather than a mutable label alone.

steps.label: 3. Deploy the exact artifact to staging
steps.detail: Functional and security tests validate the same bytes that can later reach production.

steps.label: 4. Apply automated and manual gates
steps.detail: Metrics, tests, and required approval determine whether the release advances.

steps.label: 5. Promote without rebuilding
steps.detail: Production receives the already-verified artifact identity, avoiding environment-specific rebuild drift.

drillDefinitions.title: Package event before polling
drillDefinitions.prompt: CodeArtifact emits EventBridge events when package versions are created, modified, copied, retained, or deleted. A release rule can match the repository, package, version state, and operation, then start CodePipeline directly. Consumers must tolerate duplicate or out-of-order events.

explanation.concise: CodeArtifact ya produce el evento; no se necesita un cron que pregunte continuamente si apareció una versión.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Filtrar el evento correcto reduce latencia y ejecuciones inútiles.

drillDefinitions.title: Event-driven package pipeline
drillDefinitions.prompt: A shared Java library is published to CodeArtifact several times per week. A validation pipeline must start only when a new version of package com.example:pricing reaches the Published state. Which solution is MOST efficient?

answerOptions.label: Create an EventBridge rule that matches CodeArtifact package-version events for the repository, package, and Published state, and target CodePipeline.
Run a Lambda function every minute to list every package version in every repository.
Configure an S3 event on the CodePipeline artifact bucket.
Create a CloudWatch alarm on repository storage size.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Polling can discover new versions.
distractorMetadata.failure: It adds repeated list calls and state tracking when CodeArtifact already emits the event.

distractorMetadata.attraction: S3 can trigger events for new objects.
distractorMetadata.failure: The authoritative event is package publication in CodeArtifact, not a pipeline artifact-bucket write.

distractorMetadata.attraction: CloudWatch alarms automate responses to metrics.
distractorMetadata.failure: Repository size does not identify a specific published package version.

explanation.concise: Package + Published + only when apunta a un EventBridge pattern sobre CodeArtifact.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A inicia exactamente el flujo requerido sin polling.

drillDefinitions.title: Order a package promotion workflow
drillDefinitions.instructions: Place the operational steps in the correct order.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A company promotes validated packages from a development repository to a production repository.

workflowItems.label: Publish the version to the development repository with immutable version metadata.
Match the publication event and start validation.
Run dependency, license, security, and compatibility tests.
Copy the approved package version to the production repository without rebuilding it.
Allow production builds to resolve dependencies from the production repository.

explanation.concise: Promover significa mover la misma versión validada, no compilar otra vez con el mismo nombre.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El orden conserva identidad y separa repositorio de desarrollo de repositorio aprobado.

drillDefinitions.title: Map CodeArtifact event fields
drillDefinitions.instructions: Map each component to the responsibility it owns.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Match each event field to the operational decision it supports.

answerOptions.label: Limits automation to the intended repository
Distinguishes Published from Unfinished, Unlisted, Archived, or Disposed
Identifies a changed set of package assets or metadata
Helps order package events that arrive out of sequence
Distinguishes Created, Updated, and Deleted changes

explanation.concise: El evento contiene suficiente identidad para filtrar, ordenar y deduplicar sin volver a escanear todo el repositorio.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El mapeo evita usar solo packageName y reaccionar a estados o repositorios incorrectos.

drillDefinitions.title: Eliminate duplicate package processing
drillDefinitions.prompt: A CodeArtifact-triggered pipeline occasionally processes the same package version twice because EventBridge retries delivery. Which design BEST prevents duplicate promotion?

answerOptions.label: Use package identity plus packageVersionRevision or sequenceNumber as an idempotency key and record completed processing before promotion.
Disable all EventBridge retries.
Change the package version to latest for every build.
Increase CodeBuild compute size.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Fewer retries reduce duplicate delivery.
distractorMetadata.failure: They also reduce reliability and do not eliminate all duplicate-event possibilities.

distractorMetadata.attraction: A common tag simplifies consumer configuration.
distractorMetadata.failure: A mutable alias makes identity and deduplication worse.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Larger compute can finish faster.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not change event semantics.

explanation.concise: Los flujos event-driven deben asumir at-least-once y hacer la promoción idempotente.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A identifica de forma estable la revisión ya procesada y evita repetir la acción destructiva.

drillDefinitions.title: Release only approved package versions
drillDefinitions.prompt: Development teams publish npm packages to a shared CodeArtifact development repository. Production builds must consume only versions that passed security and compatibility tests. The company wants near-real-time automation with minimal custom infrastructure. Which solution is BEST?

answerOptions.label: Use EventBridge package-version events to start a validation pipeline, then copy the exact approved package version to a production repository that production builds use as their dependency source.
Allow production builds to use the development repository and trust semantic-version ranges.
Poll the public npm registry every hour and rebuild every package.
Copy source code to S3 and let each production build generate a new package version.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Semantic versioning controls compatible version ranges.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not prove security or compatibility approval.

distractorMetadata.attraction: External repositories provide public dependencies.
distractorMetadata.failure: The authoritative packages are in CodeArtifact and the requirement is event-driven internal promotion.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Rebuilding can reproduce a package.
distractorMetadata.failure: It violates build-once promotion and can create byte drift.

explanation.concise: El repositorio de producción funciona como frontera de aprobación y recibe la misma versión validada.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A separa publicación, validación y consumo sin polling ni reconstrucción.

drillDefinitions.title: Spaced review: package release signal
drillDefinitions.prompt: Which pairing is correct?

answerOptions.label: New approved package version → CodeArtifact event through EventBridge; duplicate delivery → idempotency key
New approved package version → Route 53 health check; duplicate delivery → larger CodeBuild instance
New approved package version → S3 lifecycle rule; duplicate delivery → CloudFormation drift detection
New approved package version → scheduled manual review only; duplicate delivery → mutable latest tag

distractorMetadata.attraction: Both Route 53 and CodeBuild are operational services.
distractorMetadata.failure: Neither owns CodeArtifact package events or event deduplication.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Lifecycle and drift controls automate other domains.
distractorMetadata.failure: They do not provide the package-release signal.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Manual review can add governance.
distractorMetadata.failure: A mutable tag and no event identity make repeat processing harder.

explanation.concise: Evento de paquete e idempotencia forman el patrón completo.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A conserva señal y protección contra entrega repetida.

drillDefinitions.title: Account boundary and Region boundary
drillDefinitions.instructions: Read the two independent pipeline dimensions.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Cross-account actions require a target-account role, trust, deployment permissions, artifact-bucket access, and KMS authorization. Cross-Region actions require the action Region plus an artifact store in each Region; CodePipeline copies input artifacts for the action.

explanation.concise: Cuenta y región son dos problemas distintos que pueden coexistir.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Separarlos evita creer que roleArn resuelve replicación regional o que artifactStores resuelve trust cross-account.

drillDefinitions.title: Which account owns the deploy role
drillDefinitions.prompt: A pipeline in a tools account deploys a CloudFormation stack in a production account. Where should the role used by the cross-account deploy action live?

answerOptions.label: In the production account, trusting the pipeline service role from the tools account
Only in the tools account, trusting itself
In an unrelated logging account
No role is required if both accounts are in AWS Organizations

distractorMetadata.attraction: The pipeline service role originates in the tools account.
distractorMetadata.failure: The action role must exist where the deployment resources and permissions are owned.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Central accounts often host shared roles.
distractorMetadata.failure: An unrelated account cannot authorize production resources.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Organizations establishes account governance.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not automatically grant workload deployment access.

explanation.concise: El rol vive en la cuenta destino porque allí se autorizan los recursos de despliegue.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A establece trust desde production hacia el service role del pipeline.

drillDefinitions.title: Order a cross-account pipeline setup
drillDefinitions.instructions: Place the operational steps in the correct order.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A central pipeline must deploy an application into another AWS account.

workflowItems.label: Create or select a customer-managed KMS key for pipeline artifacts and authorize required principals.
Configure the artifact bucket policy for target-account access.
Create the target-account action role with trust for the pipeline service role and deployment permissions.
Allow the pipeline service role to assume the target-account role.
Configure the action with the target roleArn and validate artifact access.

explanation.concise: El action no funciona hasta que la identidad y el artefacto tienen autorización de ambos lados.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El orden configura primero datos y confianza antes de ejecutar la acción.

drillDefinitions.title: Map cross-boundary pipeline components
drillDefinitions.instructions: Map each component to the responsibility it owns.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Match each component to the responsibility it owns.

answerOptions.label: Orchestrates the pipeline and assumes the target role
Authorizes deployment actions in the target account
Allows the target side to access pipeline artifacts
Allows approved principals to use the artifact-encryption key
Provides an artifact bucket for each Region containing actions

mappingItems.label: KMS key policy and IAM permissions

explanation.concise: Cada fallo de autorización deja un síntoma distinto, pero todos son gates obligatorios.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El mapeo permite localizar si el error está en STS, S3, KMS o configuración regional.

drillDefinitions.title: Eliminate the alias-only KMS design
drillDefinitions.prompt: A cross-account CodePipeline action can assume the target role but cannot decrypt its input artifact. The artifact store uses a customer-managed KMS key in the pipeline account. Which correction is MOST likely required?

answerOptions.label: Authorize the target-account role in the KMS key policy and its IAM permissions, and reference the key by key ID or ARN for cross-account use.
Add more CPU to the deployment target.
Create an SCP that allows kms:* and remove all key policies.
Use only the KMS alias name from the target account.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Compute capacity can affect deployment duration.
distractorMetadata.failure: The stated failure is cryptographic authorization.

distractorMetadata.attraction: An SCP can limit or permit the possibility of actions.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not replace KMS key-policy authorization.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Aliases are convenient key identifiers.
distractorMetadata.failure: Cross-account actions require a key ID or ARN and authorization to the actual key.

explanation.concise: AssumeRole exitoso no implica decrypt exitoso; KMS es un gate separado.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A corrige key policy, IAM permissions e identidad de clave.

drillDefinitions.title: One pipeline with a cross-Region deploy action
drillDefinitions.prompt: A pipeline is hosted in eu-west-1 and must add a native CodeDeploy action in us-east-2. The company wants CodePipeline to manage artifact transfer and does not want a second polling pipeline. Which solution is BEST?

answerOptions.label: Add a cross-Region CodeDeploy action, configure an artifact store in each action Region in the pipeline account, and let CodePipeline copy the input artifact.
Create a cross-Region source action in us-east-2.
Copy the artifact manually and invoke a scheduled second pipeline.
Create only a target-account role; no regional artifact store is needed.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Source actions start pipelines from repositories.
distractorMetadata.failure: Source actions cannot be configured as cross-Region actions.

distractorMetadata.attraction: A second pipeline can deploy regional artifacts.
distractorMetadata.failure: It adds polling and coordination when one pipeline supports cross-Region native actions.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Target roles solve account boundaries.
distractorMetadata.failure: The requirement is regional artifact transfer and needs per-Region artifact stores.

explanation.concise: Cross-Region action + artifactStores permite que CodePipeline copie el input al Region destino.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A satisface una sola orquestación sin inventar un segundo pipeline.

drillDefinitions.title: Bank return: cross-account S3 deployment
drillDefinitions.instructions: Answer the referenced verified bank question without hints, then review the decisive CI/CD pattern.

explanation.concise: El retorno obliga a construir la ruta completa entre cuenta de desarrollo, rol destino, artifact bucket y KMS.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El conjunto correcto cubre identidad y cifrado/artefactos; una sola pieza no completa el flujo.

drillDefinitions.title: Buildspec and runOrder control sentence
drillDefinitions.instructions: Read what controls build behavior and pipeline concurrency.
drillDefinitions.prompt: The buildspec defines CodeBuild commands, reports, and artifacts. CodeBuild environment variables can supply branch or commit identity. In CodePipeline, independent actions with the same runOrder execute in parallel; different runOrder values execute sequentially.

explanation.concise: Buildspec controla el build; runOrder controla la dependencia entre actions del stage.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Separar ambos niveles evita intentar arreglar serialización cambiando CPU o YAML del build.

drillDefinitions.title: Parallelize independent test actions
drillDefinitions.prompt: Three network-bound test actions in one CodePipeline stage are independent but currently run one after another. Which change MOST directly reduces stage duration?

answerOptions.label: Assign the actions the same runOrder so they execute in parallel.
Increase the runOrder value of each action.
Increase only CodeBuild vCPU for every test.
Move the tests to separate manual approval actions.

distractorMetadata.attraction: runOrder defines action ordering.
distractorMetadata.failure: Different increasing values preserve sequential execution.

distractorMetadata.attraction: More compute can speed CPU-bound tests.
distractorMetadata.failure: The scenario identifies network-bound work and unnecessary serialization.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Separate actions can improve visibility.
distractorMetadata.failure: Manual approvals add delay and do not parallelize tests.

explanation.concise: Independent y network-bound elimina la necesidad de serialización y de más CPU.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A reduce la duración al máximo de las pruebas paralelas en vez de sumar sus tiempos.

drillDefinitions.title: Order a scalable test stage
drillDefinitions.instructions: Place the operational steps in the correct order.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A pipeline will add more independent functional and security test suites.

workflowItems.label: Package each suite in a repeatable CodeBuild environment or suitable short-running action.
Define common input artifacts and environment metadata.
Place independent actions in the same stage with the same runOrder.
Publish test reports, logs, and failure artifacts.
Allow the next stage only after all required actions succeed.

explanation.concise: Paralelizar sin evidencia produce velocidad pero mala operación; reports y gate completan el patrón.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El orden conserva repetibilidad, concurrencia, diagnóstico y control de promoción.

drillDefinitions.title: Map CodeBuild and pipeline controls
drillDefinitions.instructions: Map each component to the responsibility it owns.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Match each construct to the responsibility it owns.

answerOptions.label: Defines install, pre_build, build, and post_build commands
Packages the primary output files
Publishes separately named artifact sets
Supplies branch, revision, or execution identity
Controls parallel versus sequential actions inside a stage
Stores structured test or coverage results

explanation.concise: Los nombres están cerca en el pipeline, pero cada uno controla una capa distinta.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El mapeo permite diseñar outputs trazables sin crear proyectos por rama.

drillDefinitions.title: Eliminate one-build-project-per-branch
drillDefinitions.prompt: A company wants CodeBuild artifacts named by the branch under test. New branches are created frequently, and the team wants the LOWEST maintenance effort. Which approach is BEST?

answerOptions.label: Use one reusable buildspec and derive the artifact name from source or pipeline environment metadata at runtime.
Create one CodeBuild project and one hard-coded buildspec for every branch.
Rename every object manually in S3 after each build.
Use the same unversioned artifact name for every branch and overwrite it.

distractorMetadata.attraction: A project per branch allows custom settings.
distractorMetadata.failure: It creates continuous infrastructure and configuration work.

distractorMetadata.attraction: S3 object rename logic can change names.
distractorMetadata.failure: It adds a custom post-processing path when CodeBuild can name artifacts directly.

distractorMetadata.attraction: One name is simple.
distractorMetadata.failure: It destroys branch traceability and causes collisions.

explanation.concise: La metadata del source debe parametrizar el artifact en runtime.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A escala automáticamente a nuevas ramas sin nuevos proyectos.

drillDefinitions.title: Long functional tests after staging deployment
drillDefinitions.prompt: A pipeline deploys to staging and then runs functional tests that normally take more than two hours. Production deployment must occur only after the tests pass. Which design is MOST efficient?

answerOptions.label: Use a CodeBuild action after the staging deployment to run the test suite, publish reports, and allow production only after success.
Run the full suite inside one synchronous Lambda invocation.
Run the tests before staging exists.
Deploy directly to production and run tests afterward.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Lambda can run custom test code.
distractorMetadata.failure: The long duration and full test environment favor CodeBuild rather than Lambda limits.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Testing earlier is generally valuable.
distractorMetadata.failure: These functional tests explicitly target the deployed staging environment.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Post-production testing can detect issues.
distractorMetadata.failure: It violates the required pre-production gate.

explanation.concise: CodeBuild es el action nativo para suites largas y controladas después de staging.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A conserva el orden deploy staging → test → deploy production.

drillDefinitions.title: Bank return: parallel network-bound tests
drillDefinitions.instructions: Answer the referenced verified bank question without hints, then review the decisive CI/CD pattern.

explanation.concise: El retorno verifica si se identifica la serialización como causa principal.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: La respuesta correcta usa el mismo runOrder y no desperdicia esfuerzo aumentando CPU.

drillDefinitions.title: Build once and promote exact content
drillDefinitions.prompt: A release artifact should be built once, assigned immutable identity, tested in staging, and promoted to production without rebuilding. Mutable labels can remain for convenience, but a digest, version, checksum, or S3 object version should identify the deployed bytes.

explanation.concise: La promoción segura mueve el mismo contenido validado; reconstruir en producción reabre el riesgo.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Usar identidad de contenido permite auditar qué bytes llegaron a cada entorno.

drillDefinitions.title: Container tag or digest
drillDefinitions.prompt: An ECS service intermittently runs an older image when the pipeline reuses the tag latest. Which reference should the new task definition use to identify the exact image content?

answerOptions.label: The image SHA-256 digest
The mutable latest tag only
The ECS cluster name
The CodePipeline execution name without image metadata

distractorMetadata.attraction: latest is familiar and easy to read.
distractorMetadata.failure: It can point to different image content over time.

distractorMetadata.attraction: The cluster owns running tasks.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not identify container-image bytes.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Pipeline execution IDs improve traceability.
distractorMetadata.failure: Without mapping to a digest they do not tell ECS which immutable image to pull.

explanation.concise: Digest es content-addressed; latest es un alias mutable.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A elimina ambigüedad y cache inconsistency al solicitar exactamente la imagen construida.

drillDefinitions.title: Order a build-once release
drillDefinitions.instructions: Place the operational steps in the correct order.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A service moves through development, staging, and production.

workflowItems.label: Build one artifact and generate checksum, version, or digest metadata.
Store the immutable artifact in the approved repository or artifact store.
Deploy the exact identity to staging and run automated tests.
Evaluate metrics and required manual approval.
Deploy the same artifact identity to production without rebuilding.

explanation.concise: El artifact no cambia después de las pruebas; solo cambia su estado de promoción.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El orden mantiene integridad desde build hasta production.

drillDefinitions.title: Map release-artifact identity
drillDefinitions.instructions: Map each component to the responsibility it owns.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Match each artifact type to a suitable immutable identity.

answerOptions.label: Image digest
S3 object version ID and checksum
Package version and revision
Versioned artifact and template checksum
Versioned S3 object plus CloudFront invalidation or versioned path

mappingItems.label: Binary stored in a versioned S3 bucket

explanation.concise: Immutable no significa el mismo identificador para todos los servicios; significa identidad estable del contenido.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El mapeo permite rastrear releases heterogéneos con el mecanismo nativo correcto.

drillDefinitions.title: Eliminate production rebuild drift
drillDefinitions.prompt: A team builds an application separately in staging and production from the same Git commit. A production-only dependency update causes different bytes to be deployed. Which change BEST prevents this class of problem?

answerOptions.label: Build once, store an immutable artifact with version or digest metadata, and promote that exact artifact through every environment.
Keep rebuilding in each environment and compare file names.
Use the mutable latest label in every repository.
Add a manual approval before each independent rebuild.

distractorMetadata.attraction: File-name comparison can reveal obvious differences.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not prevent environment-dependent builds from producing drift.

distractorMetadata.attraction: A common label simplifies deployment configuration.
distractorMetadata.failure: Mutable identity conceals which content was validated.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Approval can govern release timing.
distractorMetadata.failure: It does not make independently built artifacts identical.

explanation.concise: El commit identifica source, no necesariamente el artifact final si dependencias y entorno cambian.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: A hace que staging y production reciban exactamente los mismos bytes.

drillDefinitions.title: Automate a generated SDK release
drillDefinitions.prompt: After each API deployment, a JavaScript SDK must be exported from API Gateway, uploaded to a versioned S3 location, and made available through CloudFront immediately. Which pipeline design is BEST?

answerOptions.label: Add a post-deployment Lambda action that exports the SDK, writes the versioned object to S3, and creates the required CloudFront invalidation or publishes a versioned path.
Ask an operator to export the SDK from the console after every release.
Run an unrelated S3 lifecycle transition.
Rebuild the entire API every five minutes whether or not a deployment occurred.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Manual export can create the correct SDK.
distractorMetadata.failure: It is not reliable automation tied to the deployment.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Lifecycle rules manage storage classes and expiration.
distractorMetadata.failure: They do not export SDKs or refresh CloudFront.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Scheduled work can eventually update clients.
